Done. Reflection summary:

What went wrong: I answered [2017,2.74] but gold was [2017,0.69]. The YEAR was correct; only the geometric-mean VALUE was wrong, and by ~4x.

Generalizable lesson (saved): A geometric mean of 0.69 is only reachable from small per-quarter values (~0.6-0.7). My 2.74 came from feeding in the ~2-3% annualized real GDP growth figures (or an annual/summary row) instead of the smaller printed per-quarter values the gold expects. The key takeaways worth keeping:

1. Magnitude sanity check — single-year geomean of quarterly GDP growth in this dataset lands well under ~1.0; if you get ~2-3 you used the wrong (annualized) row.
2. A correct MAX-year sub-answer does NOT validate the geomean value, because relative year-ordering survives a uniform row-selection error. You must independently verify the value magnitude.

Both captured: patched the `officeqa-treasury-bulletin` skill with a new "Geometric mean of QUARTERLY GDP growth across a year" subsection (full procedure + Python snippet), and updated memory with the compact magnitude sanity-check (freeing space by moving the fully-duplicated arc-elasticity detail into the skill only).
